dimensions.title: Independent evaluation: rules with a positive case
dimensions.detail: 8 SAST rules match 2–3 characters while the evidence contract requires mustContain >= 4, so no authored positive case can satisfy the validator (BLK-EVAL-01). Every other rule has one.
dimensions.nextAction: Owner picks: (a) allow the full match as evidence when it is shorter than 4 characters, (b) extend those 8 detectors with context, or (c) accept the gap in writing as a permanent limitation.

dimensions.title: Independent evaluation: rules with a negative control
dimensions.detail: A negative control has to be an authored fixture that the rule must not fire on; deriving them mechanically from each rule's own negative test would be circular and is explicitly not counted (counting rule in scripts/eval-coverage-report.mjs). Closed on 2026-10-21: all 11 universal rules (EVAL-SAST-256…264) and one ordinary-code control per language (EVAL-SAST-265…270: python, javascript, java, php, ruby, csharp), where every language-gated detector is named and must stay silent on benign, idiomatic code.
dimensions.nextAction: Continue in batches, highest false-positive risk first: high-severity lexical rules with short literals, then one control per category.

dimensions.title: Universal rules with both a positive case and a negative control
dimensions.detail: Universal rules run on every analysed file, so they carry the highest false-positive cost. All 11 now have an independent positive case and an independent negative control.
dimensions.nextAction: Keep the invariant: a new universal rule ships with both.

dimensions.title: DAST rules evaluable through the App response surface

Body rules are reachable but bounded by the clip.
